chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Salih ibn Uqba from Abu Harun al-Makfuuf who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Harun, recite poetry for me about al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' So I recited for him. He said: 'Recite as they recite,' meaning with emotion/weeping. So I recited this verse for him: 'Pass by the grave of Husayn and say to his pure bones.' He wept, then said: 'Add more.' So I recited the other poem. He wept, and I heard the weeping from behind the curtain.

When I finished, he said: 'O Abu Harun, whoever recites poetry about al-Husayn (peace be upon him), weeps, and makes ten people weep, Paradise is written for them. Whoever recites poetry about al-Husayn (peace be upon him), weeps, and makes five people weep, Paradise is written for him. Whoever recites poetry about al-Husayn (peace be upon him), weeps, and makes one person weep, Paradise is written for them. And whoever hears the mention of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and a tear the size of a fly's wing falls from his eyes, his reward is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and He will not be satisfied with less than Paradise for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting poetry about Imam Husain and making others cry?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith highlights the Shia tradition of *shi'r al-imam* (poetry of the Imam) as a devotional act that bridges the heart to the Ahl al-Bayt. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) validates the emotional resonance of poetry, establishing a graded reward system where the impact of the recitation on the audience correlates with the spiritual merit, ultimately affirming that even a single tear in remembrance of Imam Husayn (a.s.) suffices for Paradise.
